key_insight: A decision model can handle structured clinical predictions at lower cost than an LLM, but it works best when paired with LLMs rather than used alone.
clinical_relevance: For oncology workflows, a hybrid setup could route confident structured decisions to a cheaper decision model and reserve LLMs for the harder cases, reducing cost while maintaining performance.
method: Compared a decision model (Jev) with five flagship LLMs across three clinical tasks: mortality risk, Choosing Wisely questions, and colon cancer staging.
Tested standard LLM-style prompts, then applied developer-recommended input changes for staging, including medical context and task decomposition.
Evaluated a hybrid strategy where Jev handled fully confident staging decisions and LLMs handled the remainder.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, Jev lagged the LLMs on all tasks with standard inputs, but staging improved from 45.4% accuracy to 85.8% with both input changes, and the hybrid approach was non-inferior while cutting LLM costs by 33-44%.
watch_item: The main concern is that decision-model performance depends heavily on prompt/input design, so deployment would need careful validation, confidence thresholds, and workflow integration.
paper_title: Decision models can offload structured clinical tasks from large language models
